q: בן 78 עם דמנציה מתקדמת הוגדר חולה נוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות וסובל סבל משמעותי. רצונו שלא להאריך את חייו נקבע על פי הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות תקפות ובהתאם לחוק. המשפחה מבקשת החייאה. מה מנחה את ההחלטה?
o: הימנעות מהחייאה בהתאם לרצון החולה שנקבע כחוק
ביצוע החייאה בהתאם לבקשת המשפחה העכשווית
ביצוע החייאה מאחר שהחולה אינו יכול לסרב כעת
הימנעות מטיפול לפי הערכת איכות החיים של המשפחה
explanation:
במצב המתואר, **רצון החולה שנקבע לפי החוק** מנחה הימנעות מטיפול הקשור לבעיה חשוכת המרפא, לרבות החייאה. החוק מבחין בין טיפולים אלה לבין **טיפול נלווה**, שאין להפסיקו מכוח הוראה זו; אי כשרות אינה מעבירה את ההכרעה להעדפות המשפחה (עמ׳ 5, 10).
"על פי הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות שנתן שמתקיימות בהן הוראות סעיפים 33 ו-34(א);" (עמ׳ 5).
"יש להימנע מטיפול רפואי בו, הקשור לבעייתו הרפואית חשוכת המרפא, לרבות בדיקות, ניתוחים, החייאה, חיבור למכשיר הנשמה" (עמ׳ 10).
"אין להימנע מטיפול נלווה בחולה הנוטה למות כאמור בסעיף קטן (א)" (עמ׳ 10).

**א. הימנעות מהחייאה בהתאם לרצון החולה שנקבע כחוק.** נכונה, התקיימו התנאים שבסעיף 16 להימנעות מהחייאה בהתאם לרצון החולה (עמ׳ 10).
**ב. ביצוע החייאה בהתאם לבקשת המשפחה העכשווית.** שגויה, דרישת המשפחה אינה מחליפה רצון שנקבע בהנחיות תקפות (עמ׳ 5, 10).
**ג. ביצוע החייאה מאחר שהחולה אינו יכול לסרב כעת.** שגויה, הסעיף נועד במפורש לחולה שאינו בעל כשרות ומאפשר פעולה לפי רצונו שנקבע כחוק (עמ׳ 10).
**ד. הימנעות מטיפול לפי הערכת איכות החיים של המשפחה.** שגויה, הבסיס הוא רצון החולה והתנאים הרפואיים שבחוק, לא הערכת איכות חייו בידי המשפחה (עמ׳ 5, 10).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 5 ו-16, עמ׳ 5, 10.

q: An older patient has symptomatic osteoarthritis confined to one knee and has not yet tried pharmacological treatment. There is no contraindication to topical treatment. Which initial drug treatment does Hazzard recommend?
o: Diclofenac gel applied locally to the knee
Celecoxib tablets at a standard oral dose
Tramadol tablets taken by the oral route
Triamcinolone injected into the knee joint
explanation:
**Topical NSAIDs** are recommended before oral NSAIDs for knee osteoarthritis because of their pain relief and favorable adverse-effect profile (p. 787). Hazzard describes them as "first-line pharmacological therapy to treat hand and knee OA prior to starting oral NSAIDs" (p. 787).

**A. Diclofenac gel applied locally to the knee.** Correct, diclofenac gel is the named example of the recommended topical first-line approach (p. 787).
**B. Celecoxib tablets at a standard oral dose.** Wrong, oral NSAIDs follow topical treatment in this localized, previously untreated presentation (p. 787).
**C. Tramadol tablets taken by the oral route.** Wrong, tramadol is reserved for contraindications or inadequate responses to other treatments, rather than this initial topical-treatment opportunity (p. 788).
**D. Triamcinolone injected into the knee joint.** Wrong, intra-articular glucocorticoids are discussed for continuing symptoms after other measures, whereas topical NSAIDs are the first-line treatment here (pp. 787–789).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 787, 788, 789.
label: Source: hazzard marked .pdf · 787

q: אישה בת 83 עם mild cognitive impairment מובאת על ידי משפחתה לסקירת תרופות. היא נוטלת 8 תרופות וחוותה 2 falls לאחרונה. בתה מזכירה שקראה שנשים חיות בדרך כלל יותר מגברים ושואלת האם המשמעות היא שאמה תצטרך תכנון טיפול ארוך טווח. איזה גורם משפיע באופן המשמעותי ביותר על ההשלכות המעשיות של יתרון האורך-חיים הנשי בטיפול גריאטרי?
o: לנשים שיעורים נמוכים יותר של מחלות כרוניות
נשים מבלות יותר שנים בבריאות לקויה למרות תוחלת חיים ארוכה יותר
לנשים יש adherence טוב יותר לתרופות
לנשים מערכת חיסון חזקה יותר
explanation:
התשובה היא **יותר שנים של בריאות לקויה לצד הישרדות ממושכת**: פרדוקס הבריאות וההישרדות מתאר נשים שחיות יותר, אך מדווחות יותר על מחלות ומגבלות תפקודיות. הדבר רלוונטי לתכנון טיפול ממושך (עמ׳ 92).

**א. לנשים שיעורים נמוכים יותר של מחלות כרוניות.** שגויה, היתרון בהישרדות אינו מעיד על פחות תחלואה: נשים מתוארות עם יותר מחלה גופנית, מגבלות, ביקורי רופא, ימי אשפוז ותרופות (עמ׳ 92).
**ב. נשים מבלות יותר שנים בבריאות לקויה למרות תוחלת חיים ארוכה יותר.** נכונה, המקור מתאר יותר שנות חיים לא בריאות ושנות מוגבלות בקרב נשים, ולא רק בסוף החיים. ירידה קוגניטיבית, ריבוי תרופות ונפילות בתרחיש מדגישים צורך בהערכה ובתכנון אישי. נשים גם נוטות יותר להתאלמן ולחיות ללא בן זוג; יש להתכונן לצורכי תמיכה, מימון ושמירת עצמאות ולברר מטרות טיפול (עמ׳ 27, 92; יישום לתרחיש).
**ג. לנשים יש adherence טוב יותר לתרופות.** שגויה, היענות לתרופות אינה מסבירה את שאלת שנות התחלואה והמוגבלות הממושכות. אין בנתונים כאן בסיס להסיק היענות טובה יותר אצל המטופלת (עמ׳ 92; נתוני השאלה).
**ד. לנשים מערכת חיסון חזקה יותר.** שגויה, הסבר של מערכת חיסון חזקה יותר אינו עונה להשלכה התפקודית של הישרדות לצד תחלואה; המקור מציג פרדוקס מורכב עם מספר השערות ולא מנגנון יחיד מוכח (עמ׳ 92).

מקור: Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 27, 92.

q: A 73-year-old man with diabetes, mild cognitive impairment, and newly diagnosed prostate cancer attends a preoperative geriatric assessment before radical prostatectomy. He lives with his working daughter and manages medications using a pillbox. HbA1c is 7.8%, blood pressure is 145/85, and medications are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. MMSE is 24/30 with impaired executive function. Which perioperative plan addresses the postoperative cognitive risk identified by this assessment?
o: Schedule sedating medication and limit family presence to promote rest.
Retain urinary catheters and limit sensory aids to simplify postoperative care.
Arrange delirium prevention with sleep support, sensory aids, and medication review.
Prioritize uninterrupted bed rest and withhold pain treatment to preserve alertness.
explanation:
**Preoperative cognitive impairment** is a significant risk factor for postoperative delirium (p. 374). Hazzard states: “Cognitive impairment, dementia, or history of prior delirium are significant risk factors for developing delirium following surgery” (p. 374). The perioperative table responds with pain control, an optimized environment, accessible sensory aids, catheter removal, and minimization of psychoactive medications (p. 378).

**A. Schedule sedating medication and limit family presence to promote rest.** Wrong, the table recommends minimizing psychoactive medication and encouraging family at the bedside, rather than routine sedation and restricted family presence (p. 378).
**B. Retain urinary catheters and limit sensory aids to simplify postoperative care.** Wrong, the table calls for accessible vision and hearing aids and catheter removal, not retaining catheters and limiting sensory aids (p. 378).
**C. Arrange delirium prevention with sleep support, sensory aids, and medication review.** Correct, the proposed bundle follows the source's delirium/cognitive-impairment strategies and addresses the risk identified by his cognitive assessment (pp. 374, 378).
**D. Prioritize uninterrupted bed rest and withhold pain treatment to preserve alertness.** Wrong, the table includes pain control and early mobilization in postoperative care; withholding analgesia and prioritizing bed rest do not follow that plan (p. 378).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 374, 378.
ref: Hazzard Ch 27 — PERIOPERATIVE CARE: EVALUATION AND MANAGEMENT

q: During a safety review of lithium in an older patient with dementia, which characteristic explains concern about confusion and falls during treatment?
o: A wide therapeutic window with a reduced risk of confusion
A narrow therapeutic window with risks of toxicity and confusion
A wide therapeutic window with a reduced risk of falls
A narrow therapeutic window with a reduced risk of falls
explanation:
**Lithium’s narrow therapeutic window** has limited its use in dementia. The source links this limitation to adverse effects that include toxicity, increased falls, and confusion. (p. 931)
"its narrow therapeutic window, leading to adverse effects including toxicity, increased falls, and confusion in prior case reports and trials." (p. 931)

**A. A wide therapeutic window with a reduced risk of confusion.** Wrong, the source describes a narrow therapeutic window and confusion as an adverse effect, not a protective effect. (p. 931)
**B. A narrow therapeutic window with risks of toxicity and confusion.** Correct, this combines the narrow therapeutic window with the toxicity and confusion reported in the source. (p. 931)
**C. A wide therapeutic window with a reduced risk of falls.** Wrong, the source reports a narrow therapeutic window and increased falls rather than protection from falls. (p. 931)
**D. A narrow therapeutic window with a reduced risk of falls.** Wrong, the window is correctly described, but increased falls are a reported adverse effect. (p. 931)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 931.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 79-year-old woman with COPD, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment lives alone. She uses her albuterol inhaler “when I remember” and reports difficulty with inhaler technique. Her daughter finds expired inhalers and reports two hospitalizations for exacerbations in six months. FEV1 is 48% predicted. Her medications are as-needed albuterol MDI, daily tiotropium HandiHaler, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Which intervention addresses her difficulty delivering inhaled bronchodilators?
o: Increase the number of handheld-inhaler doses while retaining the existing delivery technique.
Add oral roflumilast in place of adapting bronchodilator delivery to her practical difficulties.
Use nebulized bronchodilators and arrange the help needed for preparation and cleaning.
Use oral theophylline as the preferred response to difficulty operating handheld inhalers.
explanation:
**Nebulizer delivery** is the easiest delivery method described when cognitive or functional impairment limits handheld-inhaler use. This addresses the delivery problem in the stem, but the device still requires preparation, maintenance, and cleaning; the support arrangement must reflect those tasks (p. 1255). "When cognitive or functional impairments limit the use of handheld inhalers, a nebulizer is the easiest delivery device to use." (p. 1255).

**A. Increase the number of handheld-inhaler doses while retaining the existing delivery technique.** Wrong, poor coordination can produce suboptimal delivery to the lungs; increasing prescribed doses without addressing technique leaves that identified barrier in place (p. 1255).
**B. Add oral roflumilast in place of adapting bronchodilator delivery to her practical difficulties.** Wrong, roflumilast is described as maintenance treatment for exacerbations despite standard inhaled bronchodilator therapy, rather than as a replacement for an effective bronchodilator delivery method (p. 1254).
**C. Use nebulized bronchodilators and arrange the help needed for preparation and cleaning.** Correct, the device choice follows the source recommendation for cognitive or functional limitations, and the planned assistance addresses its practical demands (p. 1255).
**D. Use oral theophylline as the preferred response to difficulty operating handheld inhalers.** Wrong, theophylline is not recommended for routine COPD management because of its narrow therapeutic range, limited efficacy, and adverse effects; it is not the preferred delivery adaptation described here (pp. 1254–1255).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1255, 1254.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp.1248, 1254–1255

q: Initial testing has not identified the cause of anemia in an older woman. When is the term unexplained anemia of the elderly appropriate?
o: When low hemoglobin is accompanied by advanced age at presentation
When an evaluation for the causes of anemia identifies no cause
When a normal MCV is used to omit testing for nutritional deficiencies
When established chronic kidney disease explains the reduction in hemoglobin
explanation:
**Unexplained anemia of the elderly** is used after evaluation fails to identify a cause, rather than as an explanation based on age. Hazzard states: "If none of the above causes can be found, the anemia is defined as unexplained anemia of the elderly (UAE)" (p. 1480). Initial testing assesses common causes, with further investigations considered when those tests are unrevealing (p. 1480).

**A. When low hemoglobin is accompanied by advanced age at presentation.** Wrong, advanced age does not satisfy the source’s requirement that the recognized causes have not been found (p. 1480).
**B. When an evaluation for the causes of anemia identifies no cause.** Correct, failure to identify a cause after evaluation matches the definition in the source (p. 1480).
**C. When a normal MCV is used to omit testing for nutritional deficiencies.** Wrong, the initial work-up includes iron and vitamin testing; a normal MCV does not substitute for that evaluation (p. 1480).
**D. When established chronic kidney disease explains the reduction in hemoglobin.** Wrong, kidney disease that explains the anemia supplies an identified cause, so the anemia is not unexplained under this definition (p. 1480).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1480.
ref: Hazzard Ch 94 — AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA
chapterTitle: AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA

q: In a patient with polycythemia vera, which description of thrombotic risk agrees with Hazzard?
o: Predisposition to arterial thrombosis with protection from venous thrombosis.
Predisposition to venous thrombosis with protection from arterial thrombosis.
Predisposition to thrombosis in both the arteries and the veins.
Protection from thrombosis in both the arteries and the veins.
explanation:
**Polycythemia vera** is associated with both arterial and venous thrombosis. The source also explains that polycythemia produces blood hyperviscosity, altering blood flow and increasing thrombotic risk (p. 1516).
"Myeloproliferative neoplasms including polycythemia vera and essential thrombocythemia are frequently associated with both arterial and venous thrombosis." (p. 1516).

**A. Predisposition to arterial thrombosis with protection from venous thrombosis.** Wrong, venous thrombosis is part of the reported association, so protection of the venous circulation is not supported (p. 1516).
**B. Predisposition to venous thrombosis with protection from arterial thrombosis.** Wrong, arterial thrombosis is also associated with polycythemia vera, so the proposed arterial protection is incorrect (p. 1516).
**C. Predisposition to thrombosis in both the arteries and the veins.** Correct, both circulations are included in the source description of thrombosis in myeloproliferative neoplasms (p. 1516).
**D. Protection from thrombosis in both the arteries and the veins.** Wrong, polycythemia vera is associated with thrombosis in both circulations, rather than protection in either (p. 1516).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1516.
ref: Hazzard Ch 88 — CANCER AND AGING: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

q: An older patient with a pressure injury is undernourished and has inadequate food intake. Which nutritional approach supports healing according to Hazzard?
o: Provide high-dose vitamins in place of additional energy and protein
Provide additional energy and protein, with supplements matched to nutritional deficits
Restrict protein and tighten dietary restrictions to help the wound heal
Reduce oral supplements and routinely favor tube feeding for nutrition
explanation:
**Undernutrition** is associated with pressure-injury severity and prolonged healing. Hazzard supports additional protein and energy, preferably by mouth, while distinguishing this from vitamin or mineral supplementation in people without a specific deficiency. (p. 692)
"Evidence on the efficacy of extra protein and energy via oral supplements is substantial." (p. 692)
"The preferred method of feeding is orally" (p. 692)

**A. Provide high-dose vitamins in place of additional energy and protein.** Wrong, vitamins do not implement the supported energy-and-protein supplementation strategy; the source finds no healing evidence for vitamin or mineral supplements without a corresponding deficiency. (p. 692)
**B. Provide additional energy and protein, with supplements matched to nutritional deficits.** Correct, this addresses inadequate intake using the energy-and-protein approach supported by the source and allows supplementation for nutritional deficiencies. (p. 692)
**C. Restrict protein and tighten dietary restrictions to help the wound heal.** Wrong, the source supports extra protein and modification of restrictions that reduce intake, rather than further restrictions. (p. 692)
**D. Reduce oral supplements and routinely favor tube feeding for nutrition.** Wrong, oral feeding is preferred, and tube feeding has not consistently produced positive results in people with pressure injuries. (p. 692)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 692.

q: בת 66, אלמנה תשושה בתפקודה, מתגוררת בביתה, הופנתה למחלקה לרפואה דחופה עקב חום ושועל טורדני, במיון בהכרה מלאה, נמדד חום 38.5, סטורציה 97% באוויר חדר, לחץ דם 96/54, דופק 100 לדקה, 25 נשימות לדקה, ללא שימוש בשרירי עזר. בהאזנה לריאות קרפיטציות בבסיס ריאה שמאלית. צילום חזה מצורף בתמונה מספר 11. בבדיקות מעבדה לויקוציטים 11000 עם סטייה שמאלה, המוגלובין תקין, קריאטינין 1.2, BUN 32. 14. מה ה- CURB65?
explanation:
**CURB-65** assigns one point for each present criterion. Age, diastolic blood pressure and the stated BUN yield three points here; confusion is absent and respiratory rate is below the threshold. Fever and pulse are not additional components (Hazzard 8e, p. 1686).
“A POINT IS APPLIED FOR EACH ITEM PRESENT” (p. 1686).

**A. 2.** Wrong, this omits a present criterion: age 66, diastolic pressure 54 and the BUN stated as 32 each contribute a point (p. 1686; application to the stem).
**B. 3.** Correct, three criteria are present. Full alertness does not add a confusion point, and 25 breaths per minute does not reach the threshold of 30 (p. 1686).
**C. 4.** Wrong, an additional criterion would be needed. Systolic and diastolic blood pressure belong to one component, and neither confusion nor a qualifying respiratory rate is documented (p. 1686).
**D. 5.** Wrong, this requires all five components; neither confusion nor a respiratory rate of at least 30 per minute is described (p. 1686).

Note: The stem contains corrupted wording for fever and troublesome cough and an ambiguous BUN entry with an extra number after 32. The calculation uses the BUN stated as 32 and does not interpret the extra number as a laboratory result.

Table 105-4 gives a CURB-65 score of 3, corresponding to the official answer (Hazzard 8e, p. 1686).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1686, Table 105-4 (PDF p. 1720), checked as an image. The historical official locator is Hazzard 7e, p. 1964; this explanation uses the same point explicitly stated on the checked eighth-edition page, without mapping seventh-edition pagination.
keySource: IMA 2022-Jun Subspecialty official answer key, Q95

explanationSource.note: Source-supported explanation only; official 7e citation retained without page mapping

q: בן 72, סובל ממחלת פרקינסון כ-7 שנים. למטופל תגובה טובה לטיפול ב- Dopicar, הבאה לידי ביטוי בשיפור ניכר בתפקוד המוטורי. יחד עם זאת בזמן שמתפקד היטב ישנן תנועות לא רצוניות מרובות (Peak dose Dyskinesias) הפוגעות באופן קשה באיכות חייו של. המטופל איזו מבין הגישות הטיפוליות הבאות יכולה להקל על המטופל לשמור על התפקוד היום יומי ובמקביל להפחית את התנועות הלא רצוניות ?
o: פיזיותרפיה מכוונת לשעות של הדיסקינזיות
עליה במינון ה Dopicar
הפסקת הטיפול ב Dopicar
מתן רציף של Levodopa/carbidopa בעזרת משאבה ישירות למעי
explanation:
**Peak-dose dyskinesia** occurs at peak levodopa concentrations; the goal is to preserve motor benefit while reducing fluctuations, rather than give a larger dose. Reducing each dose and giving smaller doses more frequently is described in Hazzard (p. 946). In a randomized trial, **continuous intestinal infusion** reduced dyskinesia versus optimized oral treatment and improved "on" time without troublesome dyskinesia (Freire-Alvarez et al., 2021, Abstract and Conclusions).

**A. Physiotherapy scheduled during dyskinesia.** Wrong, physiotherapy helps range of motion, mobility, and gait training; as an applied inference, scheduling it during dyskinesia does not itself correct the medication peak described here (Hazzard 8e, pp. 946, 948).
**B. Increase the Dopicar dose.** Wrong, when dyskinesia occurs at peak levodopa concentration, the source proposes reducing the individual dose; increasing it does not fit this mechanism (p. 946).
**C. Stop Dopicar.** Wrong, the stem describes motor benefit from treatment. As an applied inference, stopping it would not preserve that benefit; the source proposes adjusting dose and frequency instead of abandoning useful therapy (pp. 945-946).
**D. Continuous intestinal levodopa/carbidopa by pump.** Correct, this preserves levodopa treatment while reducing troublesome dyskinesia; the trial demonstrated improvement in both components of the question's goal (Freire-Alvarez et al., 2021, Abstract and Conclusions).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 945-946, 948; Freire-Alvarez et al. Movement Disorders. 2021;36:2615-2623, Abstract and Conclusions, doi:10.1002/mds.28703.

q: על פי המאמר Advanced dementia מאת Mitchell, מהם הסיבוכים הקליניים השכיחים ביותר בדמנציה מתקדמת?
o: הפרעות הליכה ואפתיה
הפרעות שינה והתפתחות פצעי לחץ
הפרעות אכילה וזיהומים
דיכאון ואי שליטה על סוגרים
explanation:
The article distinguishes **features of advanced dementia** from complications requiring management decisions. Eating problems and infections are the principal common complications described; a single mechanism or an allegation about nursing care is not needed to explain the choice (Mitchell, Key Clinical Points and Clinical Course).
“The most common clinical complications are eating problems and infections” (Key Clinical Points).

**A. Gait impairment and apathy.** Wrong, loss of walking ability is a feature of advanced functional impairment; this pair is not the most common complication group identified (Key Clinical Points).
**B. Sleep disturbances and pressure ulcers.** Wrong, pressure ulcers are important, but the article does not identify this pair as the commonest complications or establish that an ulcer proves neglect (Key Clinical Points; Clinical Complications).
**C. Eating problems and infections.** Correct, this is the pair explicitly named in the summary; the clinical-course discussion also describes febrile episodes and pneumonia (Key Clinical Points; Clinical Course).
**D. Depression and incontinence.** Wrong, urinary and fecal incontinence are features of advanced dementia rather than the pair identified as its commonest clinical complications. This does not mean depression is impossible (Key Clinical Points).

Source: Mitchell SL. Advanced Dementia. N Engl J Med. 2015;372:2533–2540. doi:10.1056/NEJMcp1412652, Key Clinical Points, Clinical Course and Clinical Complications.
ref: Mitchell SL. Advanced dementia. N Engl J Med.

q: מה מהבאים לא מהווה אינדיקציה לניתוח כריתת בלוטות הפאראתירואיד
o: CCT < 60 mL/min
העדפות המטופל
צפיפות עצם עם T-Score = -2.1
סידן באיסוף שתן 24 שעות< 400 מ"ג
explanation:
**Parathyroidectomy** is considered according to symptoms, patient preferences, and skeletal or renal involvement. Table 97-10 gives a skeletal threshold of a T-score below -2.5, so -2.1 alone does not meet it; creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min does meet a renal criterion (Hazzard 8e, p. 1539).
"Bone mineral density by DXA T-score < −2.5 at any site" (p. 1539).

**A. Creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min.** Wrong, the question asks for something that is not an indication, whereas this is a listed renal indication (p. 1539).
**B. Patient preferences.** Wrong, preferences are explicitly included among the indications and are not the requested exception (p. 1539).
**C. Bone density with a T-score of -2.1.** Correct, officially accepted: this value is not below -2.5 and does not alone meet the bone-density criterion (p. 1539).
**D. Urinary calcium below 400 mg in 24 hours.** Wrong, for official scoring this option was not accepted. Clinically, however, the table lists calcium excretion above 400 mg/24 h because of nephrolithiasis risk; the option's below wording does not match that indication (p. 1539).

The accepted bone-density option does not meet Table 97-10's threshold: the printed skeletal cutoff is below -2.5, not -2.1. Creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min, patient preferences, and urinary calcium above 400 mg/day are included in the table (Hazzard 8e, p. 1539).
Note: The urinary-calcium option says below 400 mg/day, whereas the table lists above that threshold. As written, this option also fails to describe the table's indication. Official scoring is preserved.
Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, p. 1539, Table 97-10.

q: בן 80 שהתקבל לחדר מיון, עקב חום וקוצר נשימה, בבדיקתו מבולבל, מתנשם כ -32 נשימה לדקה, ל"ד 95/50, במעבדה לויקוציטוזיס, עם סטייה שמאלה, CRP מוגבר, BUN = 18mg/dL, Creatinine = 1.6 mg/dL, Na = 125mmol/L. צילום חזה הצללה בריאה ימנית. באבחנת דלקת ריאות מה מומלץ על פי ציון CURB-65 במטופל זה?
o: ציון 2 – שחרור עם טיפול תוך ורידי
ציון 3 - אשפוז במחלקה פנימית
ציון 4 – אשפוז ביחידה מוגברת
ציון 5 - אשפוז ביחידה מוגברת
explanation:
**CURB-65 is 4** in this case: confusion, respiratory rate of 32 per minute, diastolic pressure of 50 mm Hg and age 80 each contribute one point. The source thresholds are a respiratory rate of at least 30, systolic pressure below 90 or diastolic pressure at most 60, and age at least 65. BUN of 18 mg/dL does not exceed the threshold of 20 mg/dL and adds no point; sodium and creatinine are not CURB-65 components. This is a calculation from the stem using the table. Scores of 4–5 indicate high mortality risk and admission with consideration of intensive care (Hazzard 8e, p. 1686).

**A. Score 2 — discharge with intravenous treatment.** Wrong, this omits two of the four present components and does not support the proposed discharge (p. 1686; calculation).
**B. Score 3 — admission to an internal medicine ward.** Wrong, this misses one of the four present components; the diastolic pressure supplies a point even though the systolic pressure does not meet its threshold (p. 1686; calculation).
**C. Score 4 — admission to a higher-acuity unit.** Correct, four components are present and BUN is below its threshold. The book recommends admission and consideration of intensive care for this score group (p. 1686).
**D. Score 5 — admission to a higher-acuity unit.** Wrong, the fifth point would require an elevated urea component. BUN of 18 is not above 20 mg/dL (p. 1686; calculation).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1686, Table 105-4.

q: בן 75, עם הפרעה בתפיסה מרחבית ובתפקודים ניהוליים מזה שנה, מינימנטל 18 בבדיקה לפני 3 חודשים וכעת מינימנטל 25. זקוק לעזרה בניהול התרופות וכספיו בחצי שנה האחרונה. סובל מהזיות ראייה ותנועות מרובות מתוך שינה. מתוארים שינויים ניכרים במצבו במהלך היום. בבדיקה ניכרת ריגידיות, ברדיקינזיה ואורטוסטטיזם. שיפור משמעותי בתסמיניו עם טיפול ב- DONEPAZIL במינון 10 מ"ג. סבל מהחמרה מוטורית קשה קשה בניסיון טיפולי עם QUANTAPINE (SEROQUEL) במינון 25 מ"ג. מהי האבחנה הסבירה ביותר?
o: Possible Dementia With Lewy Bodies - ייתכן שמדובר בדמנציה מסוג Lewy Body אבל אינו ממלא מספיק קריטריונים
Probable Dementia With Lewy Bodies - ככל הנראה מדובר בלואי בודי דמנציה
Probable Parkinson’s Disease Dementia - סביר שמדובר בדמנציה של פרקינסון מכיוון שחלפה שנה מהתחלת תסמיניו הקוגניטיבים
Possible Parkinson’s Disease Dementia - ייתכן שמדובר בדמנציה של פרקינסון לאור הופעת ההזיות בתחילת המחלה
explanation:
Official answer: ב

**Probable dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)** fits the combination of cognitive fluctuation, visual hallucinations and parkinsonism. Two core features suffice for this probability category. Antipsychotic sensitivity and response to donepezil are described in the source; these treatment responses should not be called biomarkers (p. 984).

**A. Possible DLB because insufficient criteria are met.** Wrong, the case has several core features, exceeding the requirement for probable disease rather than a lower probability based on one finding (p. 984).
**B. Probable DLB.** Correct, this official answer fits recurrent visual hallucinations, fluctuation and parkinsonism together with cognitive decline that impairs function (p. 984).
**C. Probable Parkinson disease dementia because a year has passed since cognitive symptoms began.** Wrong, elapsed time since cognitive symptoms is not the defining chronology. The source describes cognitive deterioration in established motor Parkinson disease, usually years later; that sequence is not given here (p. 984).
**D. Possible Parkinson disease dementia because hallucinations appeared early.** Wrong, early hallucinations do not shift the diagnosis to Parkinson disease dementia. With fluctuation and parkinsonism they support DLB here; Parkinson disease dementia requires preceding established Parkinson disease (p. 984).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 984.

q: Why are age-specific cancer treatment estimates uncertain?
o: Older adults are overrepresented in treatment trials
Most treatment standards were developed primarily in older adults
Trial participation matches the age distribution of cancer diagnoses
Older adults are underrepresented in treatment trials
explanation:
Older adults are disproportionately underrepresented in trials from which cancer treatment standards are derived (p1435).

A. Older adults are overrepresented in treatment trials: The book states that older adults are disproportionately underrepresented (p1435).
B. Most treatment standards were developed primarily in older adults: The treatments were developed primarily in younger adults (p1435).
C. Trial participation matches the age distribution of cancer diagnoses: The proportions of older adults in trials are lower than their proportions among cancer diagnoses (p1435).
